# Policymaker report, iteration 0091

## What changed and why
- POC step 1 (#465) ended `partial` on the input budget. It used 864k input tokens in 15 turns (codex gpt-6.1-sol).
- The saved work is tag `iter/0090/465` (commit 2708534). It has only `docs/research/poc/README.md`.
- Measured result: `pylavi/tests/add.vi` (sha256 cf4b1f56…) has save version 21008000. Its BDHb block diagram payload decompresses with zlib to an 842-byte heap.
- The heap is not decoded. No node, primitive, constant or wire is identified. No byte patch is specified. `inspect_vi.py` was not written.
- I ordered `poc-heap-decode-step2` (researcher, high effort, 120 min, 60 turns). It starts from the saved tag. It writes `inspect_vi.py`, parses the heap as a tag tree, and compares it with other pylavi VIs. It names one candidate logic change.
- Expected gain: a `heap-decode: yes|partial|no` line in the README with evidence. The next session reads this line.
- The order has a tight read budget (below 350k input tokens, small outputs), because step 1 used almost all of the input ceiling.
- I updated `policy/working-memory.md` (section Iteration 0091).

## Limits
- No LabVIEW ran. Opening without a broken arrow, behaviour and save version after an edit stay owner checks.
- The POC is not a product and not a quality measurement. Product quality stays unmeasured. Missing coverage stays explicit.
- Benchmark work that the POC does not need (for example the split allocator re-review #446) stays paused.

## What next
- `heap-decode: yes` or `partial` with a concrete field: order the edit step. It makes a patched copy, re-encodes the file, keeps the save version, and writes an owner check instruction.
- `heap-decode: no`: write the POC report for the owner with the evidence and the possible exits.
- Do not repeat the step 1 container measurements.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
